title: Counting from President Wee Kim Wee or President Ong Teng Cheong for Reserved Presidential Election − Policy Decision or Legal Question?
what_it_is: Counting from President Wee Kim Wee or President Ong Teng Cheong for Reserved Presidential Election − Policy Decision or Legal Question?

sections.label: Head of State installation circumstances
sections.summary: The passage states that the circumstances under which the Government installed her as Head of State left Singaporeans reeling.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Yet, despite her personal attributes, the lightning circumstances under which this Government installed her as the Head of State have left Singaporeans reeling in its wake.

sections.label: Question on misleading statements
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Prime Minister, Deputy Prime Minister Teo Chee Hean and Minister Chan Chun Sing made misleading statements to the House.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To cut to the chase, did the Prime Minister, Deputy Prime Minister Teo Chee Hean and Minister Chan Chun Sing make misleading statements to the House that the question of which President to count from was a legal question?

sections.label: Counting from Wee Kim Wee
sections.summary: The passage states the Government will legislate to count from Dr Wee Kim Wee, making the next election a reserved Malay election.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Government intends to legislate when we amend the Presidential Elections Act in January next year." "We have taken the Attorney-General's (AG's) advice.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We will start counting from the first President who exercised the powers of the Elected President, in other words, Dr Wee Kim Wee.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: That means we are now in the fifth term of the Elected Presidency." "…Therefore, by the operation of the hiatus-triggered model, the next election, due next year (2017), will be a reserved election for Malay candidates." Unquote.

sections.label: Teo on publishing advice
sections.summary: The passage states Deputy Prime Minister Teo told the House he would ask the Prime Minister to consider publishing the advice.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Deputy Prime Minister Teo then told the House that he would ask the Prime Minister to consider publishing the advice.

sections.label: Chan rejects assertion on advice
sections.summary: The passage states Minister Chan Chun Sing rejected the assertion and told the House the Government decided not to publish the AGC's advice.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: When I put it to the Government that counting from President Wee Kim Wee was "an arbitrary and deliberate decision to achieve a desired outcome", Minister Chan Chun Sing rejected my assertion.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: He told the House that the Government had decided not to publish the AGC's advice.

sections.label: Advice on amendment unconstitutional
sections.summary: The passage states the advice received was that Parliament's amendment to count reserved Presidential Elections from President Wee Kim Wee was unconstitutional.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The advice received was that Parliament's amendment to the Presidential Elections Act to count reserved Presidential Elections from President Wee Kim Wee was unconstitutional.

sections.label: Deputy AG on Prime Minister's statement
sections.summary: The Deputy AG told the High Court the Prime Minister never said the AG advised starting the count from President Wee.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Before the High Court on 29 June 2017, the Deputy AG said: "The Prime Minister never said that the AG advised the Prime Minister to start the count from President Wee.

sections.label: Judge sceptical of convenience argument
sections.summary: A Judge doubted the Prime Minister would use terms for convenience, yet the Deputy AG calls the advice irrelevant.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Indeed, the Deputy AG's submission that the Prime Minister would use terms "for convenience" drew some scepticism from one of the Judges, who remarked from the Bench that the Prime Minister was speaking in a Parliamentary debate and would not refer to the Elected President "for ease of convenience".

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Yet, the Deputy AG says in Court that the advice is "irrelevant".

sections.label: Government handling of Parliamentary debates
sections.summary: The Government's handling of Parliamentary debates on legislative changes for a Reserved Presidential Election was most unsatisfactory.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Government's handling of the Parliamentary debates on the legislative changes for a Reserved Presidential Election has been most unsatisfactory.

sections.label: AGC advice to legitimise Government aims
sections.summary: The Deputy AG said the AGC's advice was sought to legitimise what the Government wanted, citing policy objectives.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Be that as it may, the Deputy AG has now told us that the AGC's advice was merely sought to legitimise what the Government itself wanted to do.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: First, the Government has been always very clear and upfront on the policy objectives of this hiatus-triggered reserved elections framework.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: It has been 46 years since we have had a Malay President and our challenge was how to achieve both meritocracy and multiracialism where qualified candidates from different races can regularly be elected to be our Head of State.

sections.label: Counting as Parliament policy matter
sections.summary: The Government was clear that counting is a policy matter for Parliament, and the Government can decide.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Second, the Government has always been clear that when it comes to the counting, it is a policy matter for Parliament to decide.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: What was my reply? "The most direct answer is actually, the Government can decide.

sections.label: Constitutional text and Prime Minister's speech
sections.summary: The constitutional text lets Parliament choose any of five terms, and the Prime Minister's speech showed Parliament intended discretion.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: First, the constitutional text is clear that Parliament can choose from any of the five terms preceding the 2017 elections.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Second, the Prime Minister's speech in Parliament on the constitutional amendments made it clear that Parliament intended to give itself the discretion to specify the last term of President Wee as the first term to be counted for purposes of deciding whether an election is reserved.

sections.label: Counting from next elections
sections.summary: The Prime Minister said counting starts from here, the next elections will be reserved for a Malay President, with AGC advice taken.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: That was, I think, on the CNA transcript.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: So, the Prime Minister was entirely right to say: we will start counting from here, the next elections will be reserved for a Malay President and we have taken advice from AGC.

sections.label: Government explained reserved election approach
sections.summary: The Government set out its approach on reserved elections through the Prime Minister's instructions, a letter, the Constitutional Commission and the White Paper.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The Government made it clear, right from the time when the Prime Minister issued instructions, in terms of within Cabinet and then set out a letter explaining what he wanted to do, the terms of reference; and then, when the Constitutional Commission was set up, he also explained to the public that having a minority representation is an important issue and he wants the Constitutional Commission to consider that issue, amongst other issues.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The Government made clear in the White Paper exactly what its approach was, including on the reserved elections.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I said on record − and I am happy to be shown any other part; Ms Lim suggests that I said something else, somewhere else − that is quite untrue, I am very clear and careful about what I say and I am happy to be confronted with anything else I might have said.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I said: this is a policy matter for us to decide.

sections.label: Parliament decides, AGC advice taken
sections.summary: The Prime Minister said Parliament decides but took AGC's advice, and Parliament is sovereign.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The Prime Minister took the same position; he explained in Parliament: we decide, but we took AGC's advice.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Did anyone say: "We are going to decide this way because this is the way that AGC has told us that we have to decide"?

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: That would make no sense, because Parliament is sovereign.

sections.label: Counting from Wee Kim Wee
sections.summary: The time allowed expired, and counting starts from the first President who exercised the Elected President's powers, Dr Wee Kim Wee.

sentences.speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
sentences.text: The time allowed for the proceedings has expired —

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We will start counting from the first President who exercised the powers of the Elected President" − so, no rewriting of history here − that was "Dr Wee Kim Wee.
